endTime_ground: the parent chain ran 30000 iterations on a 50 D domain; this domain is 1.2x longer, so the same convergence per unit length needs about 1.2x the iterations. 40000 is 1.33x and leaves margin. writeInterval 2000 is kept STRICTLY less than endTime (L-140).

D_Ts_Re25_U_c.cap_ground: 3.2x the parent-rate POINT. A SCRATCH PROBE of this arm's own c case, run through run_one_dts_u.sh on 2026-08-26 (200 iterations, rc 0), measured 6.494e-06 core-s per cell-iteration -- 2.27x the parent's own measured c-level rate, on a box carrying several other teams' solves at the time. The POINT stays the PARENT-MEASURED figure (the honest estimate of the work); the CAP is sized to absorb that contention factor with margin, because rule 12 stops the run at the cap and an overrun gets no new budget.

completion.note: capped is an INFRASTRUCTURE field and never a completion conjunct (L-342). ExecutionTime line count == endTime (deltaT 1).

convergence.what: the campaign's own registered criterion, unchanged: analyse_t1c.iterative_convergence on the LAST TWO WRITTEN CHECKPOINTS, max_cells |a-b| / (max(b)-min(b)) <= 1e-6 on T and U. It is NOT the solver residual -- T1c's own docstring records a non-converged case impersonating a discretisation failure at a merely unremarkable 4e-05 residual.

cost.basis: per-level PARENT MEASURED rates: each U case is priced from the wall time its OWN parent level actually spent (dts.json completion block, wall_seconds / (cells x endTime)), so the level-to-level rate drift (2.36e-06 -> 4.17e-06 core-s per cell-iteration, cache-bound) is carried rather than averaged away
cost.usd_basis: derived, not measured, from the owner-stated c7a.4xlarge rate $0.0513/core-h (COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER section 5)
cost.corroboration: the frozen text estimated 'about 5 core-hours' for the six cases; the measured-rate POINT is 234.1 core-min = 3.90 core-h, inside that estimate

scratch_probe.source: MEASURED 2026-08-26T22:49Z on a SCRATCH COPY of the registered D_Ts_Re25_U_c, run through run_one_dts_u.sh under the queue runner's setsid/nohup/cd form with the registered dictionaries (endTime cut to 200, writeInterval 100): rc 0, wall 6 s, 200 ExecutionTime lines, two written checkpoints; mean ExecutionTime delta over iterations 22-200 = 0.03117 core-s per iteration. Outside the repository; no registered case was touched.
scratch_probe.attribution: box contention -- several teams' solves were live at the probe. Recorded here rather than folded into the POINT, so the completion calibration can attribute the gap (rule 12) instead of absorbing it.

launcher.why_new: run_one_dts.sh predates the queue runner and CANNOT be queued: its G2 guard refuses ANY process whose cwd is the case directory, with no lineage exclusion, so under the runner's `setsid nohup bash -c 'cd <cwd>; ...'` form it refuses its own launch (the T10aR2 / T4b / R_ff cwd-guard defect, 9fa66065); its G1 guard requires a LAUNCH_LOCK that only launch_dts.sh creates, and launch_dts.sh self-detaches; it enforces NO timeout, so rule 12's 'an overrun stops the run' has no mechanism; and its STATUS is a single `rc= wall= checkMesh_rc=` line carrying no capped, ranks, core_min or timeout_s. run_one_dts.sh is NOT edited and NOT deleted -- the existing arms' provenance stands on it.
launcher.guard: lineage-aware foreign-process scan (T10aR2 AMENDMENT 1, 9fa66065; the block copied from run_one_t14.sh:145-157)
